key_insight: Patch routing builds low-frustration block encodings of lattice Hamiltonians by reusing one local patch encoding through coherent SWAP-style routing.
engineering_relevance: The approach can reduce fault-tolerant quantum simulation costs by separating lattice-independent local encoding work from routing that scales linearly with lattice size.
method: Block-encode a small interaction patch using local symmetries and algebraic structure.
Coherently route the patch encoding across the lattice with a SWAP-style network.
Use larger hierarchical patches to trade higher local encoding cost for lower normalization and query complexity.
evidence_signal: For 120×120 systems, the abstract reports leading-cost reductions of 15–17× for frustrated J1–J2 Heisenberg qubitized QPE, approximately 3× for half-filled Fermi–Hubbard QPE, and 5× for honeycomb spin-liquid time evolution.
watch_item: Reported QPE savings exclude initial state preparation and overlap, while routing dominates costs at large lattice sizes.
paper_title: Low-frustration block encodings by patch routing
